name: Peanut Tofu-Cauliflower Bake with Bell Pepper, Edamame & Rice (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.

Cut tofu in half along the long side. Sandwich tofu between clean towels or paper towels and place on a large baking sheet pan. Place a cutting board with something heavy on top and set aside to press out excess water.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup jasmine rice
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.primary_message: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, place oil and spices in a medium bowl, then whisk to combine the spice paste.
instructions.secondary_message:
neutral vegetable oil
½ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp turmeric, ground
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry cauliflower; separate into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Add to the bowl with the spice paste.

Medium dice tofu, then add to the bowl and stir to combine. Wipe the baking sheet dry with paper towels, then return tofu and cauliflower to the baking sheet and spread out in an even layer. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until tofu and cauliflower are golden brown, 15-20 minutes.

Meanwhile, place peanut butter, water, maple syrup, soy sauce, vinegar, oil, and garlic powder in the reserved bowl. Whisk to combine the peanut sauce. (Add additional water, 1 tablespoon at a time if needed, to reach desired consistency.) Set aside a scant ¼-cup for the kid plates.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup natural peanut butter
2 tsp pure maple syrup
2 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp rice vinegar
1 tsp neutral vegetable oil
¼ tsp garlic powder

instructions.primary_message: Add chili-garlic sauce to the medium bowl with the remaining peanut sauce, then whisk once more to combine.
Place edamame in a colander and rinse under hot water (from the tap) to thaw. Set aside a ½-cup for the kid plates, then add remaining edamame to the medium bowl with the spicy peanut sauce.
Wash, dry, trim, and seed bell pepper; cut into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
When the tofu and cauliflower are done, set aside 1 ½ cups for the kid plates. Add remaining tofu and cauliflower to the bowl, then stir to combine.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide a ½-cup rice, reserved edamame, tofu, and cauliflower between plates. Serve with plain peanut sauce for dipping. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining rice and the spicy tofu-cauliflower between plates. Enjoy!
